title: Anchor-token normalization regression causing customer-specific eval mismatches
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers reported systematic token-level differences in evaluation outputs after the runtime change that normalizes 'anchor' termination tokens across sampling code paths. Symptoms include longer tails and unexpected JSON truncation for prompt sets that rely on custom stop sequences. Impacted environments: Hosted and Private (customer-specific sampling overrides in private pools showed the largest delta).
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Feb 13-17): Reproduced mismatch for Customer A using their eval harness. Root cause traced to the new anchor-token normalization pass in runtime-1.22: we canonicalize variants of termination markers (e.g., '\n--END--' vs '--END--') to a normalized token before sampling. That normalization was applied upstream of the sampling-config merge, which caused per-customer stop-sequence overrides (set at request or private-pool level) to be compared against already-normalized tokens and in some cases dropped or mis-ordered. The sampling fallthrough then used model defaults, changing termination timing and sampling distribution (temperature/bias interplay).
planned_fix: 1) Move anchor-token normalization to after config-merge so customer-specified stop sequences are preserved verbatim during merge and matching. 2) Add a canonical-mapping step only for logging/metrics (not sampling precedence). 3) Add unit tests + integration tests that run customer eval sets through Hosted/Dedicated/Private stacks. 4) Deploy hotfix to a small set of affected private pools and one hosted region for verification before full rollout.
qa_strategy:
- Add deterministic testcases that assert identical token-level terminations for identical prompt+config across hosted vs private pools.
- Run customer-provided eval scripts in CI against a runtime-1.22-hotfix image.
- Add a small A/B rollout metric (token-level KL divergence, JSON parse error rate, median latency) and monitor for regressions over 48 hours.
rollback_plan: If customer-facing metrics worsen post-deploy: immediate rollback to runtime-1.21 in affected regions/private pools, open incident bridge, notify customers with mitigation steps (use explicit stop tokens with unique prefix), and deploy follow-up patch within 24 hours.
customer_communications:
- Feb 14: Acknowledge receipt and initial triage to Customer A and B; provide temporary mitigation (explicit prefixed stop tokens).
- Feb 20: Shared technical root-cause and ETA for hotfix.
- Mar 11: Provided staged verification artifacts and asked for sign-off from Customer A on their eval harness.
- Ongoing: Weekly status with affected customers until final rollout.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Customer A's eval harness (provided link) with their private-pool config and sampling overrides (temperature=0.8, stop=['\n--END--']).
2) Run 5k eval prompts on runtime-1.22 and record token-level termination index and JSON parse failures.
3) Run same harness against runtime-1.21 and compare termination index distribution and parse error rate.
4) Observe that runtime-1.22 normalizes the stop to '--END--' early during merge and sampling uses model default cutoff, producing longer outputs and increased JSON failures for a subset of prompts.
